blocks.h2: Using Access Panels to Avoid Tile Work
blocks.body: Many Lincoln Park bathrooms have an access panel in a closet or hallway behind the shower wall. When there is one, we can reach the valve and pipes without touching the tile. When there isn't, we work through the valve opening in the shower wall. If a repair needs more room, we'll tell you before we cut, and suggest adding a panel so future work is easier.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Shower Repair
blocks.body: A cartridge swap is quick. Replacing an older valve costs more, especially without an access panel. Finding a leak into the unit below may need testing. We diagnose and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Shower Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Is my shower leaking into the unit below?
items.preview: We test the valve, drain and tile.
items.answer: If there's a stain below, we test the valve, the drain and the tile and grout to find the source.

items.q: Can you replace an old two-handle valve?
items.answer: Yes, with a single-handle pressure-balancing valve and a trim plate that covers the old openings.

items.q: Why does my shower turn hot when someone flushes?
items.answer: Older valves don't balance pressure. A new valve fixes it.

items.q: Can you fix a drip without opening the wall?
Can you add an access panel?
items.answer: Yes, where a wall behind the shower allows it.

items.q: Can you fix low pressure in an upper-floor shower?
items.answer: Often, by clearing scale or replacing a worn cartridge. Sometimes the supply pipe is the cause.

items.q: How much does shower repair cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the problem. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what's wrong and how we reach it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
